answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should charge every identity with work that is cheap once and ruinous at scale. A single harbor check proves almost nothing on its own, yet when that check is tied to a public dawn of vouches, penalties and timing, a cluster of fake accounts starts to stand out. Trust then accumulates the way a tide builds: slowly, in the open, and only while the same identity keeps behaving honestly over ninety days of steady activity.
